plan.name: Backlog burn-down (2026-09): feature-bug follow-ups, then harness cleanup
plan.conventions: This plan burns down the open-issue backlog left behind by the new-features plan (#396, merged as PR #426) and the harness optimization plan (#293, still finishing wave 6 in the main checkout - do not touch #293, #299 or #318, do not comment on them, this plan runs entirely from this worktree instead). Also excluded: #409 and #410 (real NAS credential provisioning and a physical deploy step, not something a coding session in a worktree can do - leave for a manual/joint session) and #361 (blocked on PR #319 merging, which is deliberately being kept open until the harness plan's remaining waves finish reading docs/plans/2026-09-harness-optimization.md from its branch - re-check gh pr view 319 --json state once wave 6 finishes, do not schedule #361 here). Every wave here runs strictly sequentially, one package at a time - not just because several harness packages touch the same shared files (CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md, the three reviewer prompts under .claude/agents, docs/specs/01-architecture-and-deployment.md: edit ONLY the section your own issue names, appending rather than reflowing, so a package never reorders or reformats a section another package owns), but because part of wave 3's own content (#377, #382, #389, #391) is two concurrent E2E gate runs on this same machine corrupting each other's stack - running one package at a time removes that risk while it is still unfixed. A package whose issue references other issue numbers besides its own specIssue must close every one of them explicitly with gh issue close <N> and a short comment saying it was fixed together with the group - the orchestrator only watches the specIssue number for this package's completion, so an issue mentioned in the focus text but never explicitly closed stays open forever. Two-review-pass cap applies as always (.claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md, the review-pass-limit convention): a finding still open after round 2 becomes a new issue, not a third round. No host toolchain - every build, test and migration runs through docker compose, per docs/specs/01-architecture-and-deployment.md. Wave 1 (feature-bug follow-ups) touches product code and must keep CLAUDE.md's silent invariants intact wherever it touches them: 404-not-403 for unknown AND inaccessible storages and the whole admin area, identical response either way; is_admin re-queried from the DB on every admin request, never returned in any JSON and never a client-side branch; debug_reason only when APP_ENV is dev, emitted from the single error serializer; same-storage validation on every id; every inventory_batches write paired, in the same transaction, with an inventory_logs row; EXIF stripped from every upload with orientation applied to pixels FIRST; expiry cascades touching derived dates only, never user ones; CACHE_VERSION in web/static/sw.js bumped on any change to a SHELL_ASSETS file's content, enforced by web/shell_manifest_test.go. Waves 2 and 3 (harness cleanup) touch none of that - they change CI, the review loop, the orchestrator and deployment tooling, not the product, so the package issue body is the contract there and docs/plans/2026-09-harness-optimization.md is context where an issue's own body references a decision (D1-D10).

packages.spec: Issue 427/428: icon-picker egress guard bug and stale spec pointer
packages.focus: Two related, non-blocking findings from PR #426 round 2 (spec 40/42, the new-features wave 1 consolidation). First and more important, #428: internal/iconlib/egress_test.go's TestIconPickerFrontendCallsOnlyItsOwnAPI scans web/static/js/icon-picker.js line by line stripping comments with stripLineComment before checking for calls to an external host; this is the third vacuous-check bug found in that function and it still misses a URL split across a multi-line template literal (read #428's own repro before touching the function - it names the exact construct that slips through). Fix stripLineComment (or replace the line-by-line scan with a full-file approach that tokenizes template literals properly) so a URL cannot hide from the check by being split across lines, and add a fixture proving it. Second, #427: docs/specs/40-icon-picker.md and docs/specs/42-local-icon-library.md both point at an E2E network-blocked check that was never written; the real guard is the Go test above. Fix the spec text to name internal/iconlib/egress_test.go directly instead of a nonexistent E2E spec. Close #428 when the guard fix and its fixture land; close this issue (#427) when the spec text is corrected.

packages.spec: Issue 418/420: container_label/container_type at batch-creation time, plus PR 419 round-1 cleanup
packages.focus: Two follow-ups to spec 39 (batch containers), deliberately deferred out of #400. Main piece, #418: docs/specs/39-batch-containers.md's own closing paragraph on 'Setting and clearing a container on a batch' says a batch can also be given a container_label/container_type at creation time, with the same upsert rule the PATCH already has - not yet built. Add the two fields to POST /api/storages/{storage_id}/inventory-batches (internal/httpapi/stocktake.go, CreateBatch) and to the vision review confirm step POST /api/storages/{storage_id}/ingest/{job_id}/confirm (internal/httpapi/ingest.go): store.NewBatch takes the two fields, and createBatch calls upsertBatchContainerLabel/setBatchContainerType (internal/store/containers.go) after its INSERT, inside the same transaction - no new inventory_logs row, same as every other container operation. Second, #420, small cosmetic fixes in internal/httpapi/batches.go: the empty-batch-PATCH 422 response repeats one sentence under four keys (tighten to one message, or give each key its own accurate one), plus a dead assignment nearby. Close #420 when its two nits are fixed.

packages.spec: Issue 413/414: shell--wide real reach and its missing Go test
packages.focus: Two follow-ups to spec 05's wide-layout default (#398/#412), both non-blocking should-fix. #414: e2e/specs/start-page.spec.js's WIDE_PAGES/PAGES lists are the only thing asserting every page renders shell--wide at 1280px, and that coverage is a non-required E2E spec - add a Go test (in the shape of web/shell_manifest_test.go or a new small test file) that reads every page's header/main and asserts shell--wide is present, so a regression fails go test ./... rather than only a best-effort E2E run. #413: docs/specs/33-inventory-overview-table.md (around line 167) says inventory.html puts shell--wide on 'both' its header and main; it is also on <nav> - correct the sentence to name all three elements, or state the rule generically. Close #414 when the Go test lands.

packages.spec: Issue 423/425: products.spec.js openProduct flake, and the missing process-as-shopping-list click
packages.focus: Two unrelated, file-disjoint E2E fixes, bundled because both are should-fix E2E gaps found while shipping spec 41. #423: e2e/specs/products.spec.js's openProduct helper flakes under the full parallel suite (12 workers), coming back red on a different test each run even on unmodified commits - not caused by any single package, but costs a review round on every PR until fixed. Read the helper's wait/selector logic and make it robust under parallel load (an explicit wait for the row's settled state rather than a race-prone click, matching whatever pattern the suite's other stable helpers already use) rather than adding a retry that hides the flake. #425: e2e/specs/mixed-classification.spec.js covers the mixed-photo banner appearing (spec 41) but never actually clicks 'Process as shopping list' and follows it through to a resolvable list - add that assertion path alongside the existing 'keep as original kind' coverage. Close #425 when the click-through path is covered.

packages.spec: Issue 394/395: SHELL_ASSETS comment-stripping, tree-modal comment drift, spec 01 serial-mode file list, and products.js vanishing save confirmation
packages.focus: Four small, file-disjoint frontend/doc fixes. From #394 (PR #392 round-1, three items): (1) web/shell_manifest_test.go's parseShellAssets strips trailing comments with a bare strings.Index(line, "//"), which would silently mis-truncate an entry containing a literal // (a protocol-relative URL) - strip only a // outside a quoted path, or reject such a line instead of guessing; (2) web/static/js/tree-modal.js: runMutation's comment (around line 315-320) and clearError's comment (around 419-425) describe the same clearing behavior in conflicting terms - review-go confirmed clearError's version is correct (the opening reload() at line ~602 bypasses runMutation and never latches a token), so rewrite runMutation's comment to defer to clearError's rather than restate its own narrower rule; (3) docs/specs/01-architecture-and-deployment.md:114-118 names only e2e/specs/barcode-recall.spec.js as using test.describe.configure({mode:'serial'}) - gamification.spec.js and stocktake.spec.js do too and behave the same way; name all three or state the rule generically. From #395: web/static/js/pages/products.js shows a 'Saved.' confirmation after a product save, then the save's own reload immediately wipes it - whether a user ever sees it depends entirely on server latency. Delay the reload (or render the confirmation in a way the reload does not clear, e.g. a toast outside the reloaded region) so it is reliably visible regardless of connection speed. Close #395 when the fix lands.

categoryShelfLife.failed is the one per-attempt banner sentence (in the category shelf-life / expiry flow) that no test exercises, flagged as unverified in both review rounds of PR #378. Find the code path that sets/reads it, and add a test that actually exercises the failure banner rendering that sentence, following the coverage style already used for its sibling per-attempt banners in the same file/area. This is a standalone test-coverage gap, unrelated to any other package in this wave - do not touch products.js, tree-modal.js or any file another package in this wave owns.

packages.spec: Issue 327/330/333: notify.ps1 thin 2-second margin, compose_test.go under-enforced guard, and issue 333 ready doc patch
packages.focus: #333 bundles four non-blocking findings from PR #331's round-1 review and must close as a whole, so this package resolves it together with the two issues it names. (a) #330: scripts/tests/hooks.test.ps1 measured scripts/hooks/notify.ps1's 2-second exit-0 fallback at ~1.5s quiet and 2.31s loaded - too thin a margin, and .claude/settings.json's own hook timeout can kill it before a toast fires. Pick one of the tradeoffs #330 documents (the cheapest: reduce Start-Job's own overhead, or raise the budget in .claude/settings.json to match a measured-safe value) and fix it. (b) #333 items 1-3: apply the ready-to-apply patch in #333's own issue body (docs/specs/01-architecture-and-deployment.md's override-mount excerpt and its CI-compose-still-unwired sentence, plus scripts/hooks/notify.ps1's and scripts/wellen-planen.md's doc comments about the 2-second margin) - adjust the patch's wording for whichever tradeoff (a) actually ships, since the patch was written assuming the margin stays thin. (c) #333 item 4 and #327 (the same finding, filed twice): cmd/inventory/compose_test.go's TestCIComposeAddsTmpfsToDatabaseOnly only asserts docker-compose.ci.yml has no app: service, but its own doc comment claims no service this package does not own - enumerate every top-level key under services: and assert db is the only one. Close #330, #333 and #327 as this work lands; this package's own specIssue is #327.

packages.spec: Issue 336/340/342: scripts/dev executable bit, pickup stale verdict-reading description, scripts/doctor refinements
packages.focus: Three small, disjoint tooling fixes. #336: git ls-files -s scripts/dev scripts/dev.d/* shows mode 100644 for every file - a bare scripts/dev <cmd> invocation from a Linux-hosted workflow or the NAS runner (not through sh) fails with 'Permission denied'. Fix: git update-index --chmod=+x scripts/dev scripts/dev.d/* and commit it. #340: .claude/skills/pickup/SKILL.md:25,32-45 still describes the pre-H5 verdict-reading mechanism (parsing **Round:**/## ... VERDICT: headers out of raw PR comment prose, no SHA scoping) - point /pickup's step 2 at scripts/dev gate <PR> (or its SHA-scoped marker reading) instead, the same way ship/SKILL.md section 6 already does. #342: three scripts/doctor refinements from PR #338's review - (1) check_ports_free (check 5, scripts/doctor:164) can't tell a stranger process from the operator's own already-running compose stack; check docker compose -p <project> ps for a service already publishing that port before reporting FAIL; (2) json_escape (scripts/doctor:335) only escapes backslash and double-quote, not embedded newline/tab - fix the POSIX-sh-portable escaping carefully, this one is fiddlier than it looks; (3) check 7 (check_git_identity_and_line_endings) derives root from $0 with no override, unlike the other three checks that read DOCTOR_SOCKET/DOCTOR_VOLUME/DOCTOR_ENV_FILE - add a DOCTOR_ROOT override so scripts/tests/doctor.test.ps1 can drive it against a synthetic CRLF fixture. Close #340 and #342 as each lands; this package's own specIssue is #336.

packages.spec: Issue 329/344/364: reviewer prompt wording, turn-budget-for-consolidation, and scripts/dev.d/packet six follow-ups
packages.focus: Opus/xhigh: this touches the three reviewer prompts under .claude/agents, which changes review behavior for every future PR - read each change against a live PR before committing to it. #329: .claude/agents/review-tests.md:48-50 claims test.yml runs 'the identical docker compose run --rm app go test ./...' as its fallback-dispatch rationale - stale since #301 changed test.yml to docker compose run --rm app sh -c 'go vet ./... && go test ./...'; fix the claim. #364: reviewer turn budgets (maxTurns 20/15/25 for go/docs/tests) are sized for a package PR; every lane overran them on wave 15's consolidation diff (14 files, ~1820 lines) - add a per-diff-size turn budget the spawning session already has the stat to compute (the same way a consolidation already gets a raised round-limit, 2 to 4), documented in whichever of the three prompts or ship/SKILL.md currently hardcodes maxTurns. #344 (six items, all in scripts/dev.d/packet and the ship skill, carried from PR #335): (1) unguarded gh/git calls at packet:79-82,111 and unchecked git diff exit status at packet:246/256/260/263 can leave a packet with a blank section while still exiting 0 - guard every one; (2) the doc-comment heuristic at packet:278 (^\+[ \t]*\/\/) only counts added comment lines, so a signature/body change under an untouched existing doc comment is false-flagged 'doc comment: no' - fix the direction of that false negative; (3) packet:323-358's H5-fallback previous-verdict lookup exists only because H5 (#304) hadn't merged when it shipped - add a comment saying so and that the branch becomes dead code once callers no longer need it; (4) ship/SKILL.md's spawn step never hands reviewers the previous round's head SHA their own step 1 tells them to use with --since - add it to the spawn step; (5) already covered by this same package - the three prompts' step 1 describe the packet's contents in different order/wording, make them consistent; (6) TestPacketSinceFindsThePreviousVerdictByTheHeaderFormat's three mustContain assertions still pass against an un-split concatenated blob a reintroduced join("") bug would produce - assert ### Previous Test review / ### Previous Docs review appear as their own sections, not just as substrings. Close #344 and #364 as each lands; this package's own specIssue is #329.

packages.spec: Issue 343/359: e2e.yml multi-dependency error message, gate unanchored SHA regex, cache restore-keys, workflow trigger coverage
packages.focus: Four CI-workflow follow-ups from waves 1-2's reviews. #343: .github/workflows/e2e.yml's image-verification step derives app's expected tag by subtracting db's images from app's resolved list; if app ever gains a second dependency the subtraction leaves more than one line and docker image inspect fails with a raw, unhelpful Docker error - check $expected is exactly one line before that call and fail with a message naming the extra images if not. #359, three items: (1) scripts/dev.d/gate:74's verdict-marker sha= regex is not anchored to [0-9a-f]{40} - a malformed/truncated SHA is silently read as a stale marker forever (permanent WAIT) instead of an explicit error; anchor it and error loudly on a non-matching sha=. (2) the actions/cache step for e2e/node_modules keys only on e2e/package.json with no restore-keys: fallback - any package.json change misses the cache completely instead of partially; add a restore-keys: prefix line. (3) .github/workflows/e2e.yml and restore.yml have no test coverage of their own trigger/path-filter shape - add a Go test in the shape of cmd/inventory/compose_test.go's YAML-text assertions, parsing the workflow files and asserting the trigger set and path filters. Close #359 as its three items land; this package's own specIssue is #343.

packages.spec: Issue 355: scripts/dev.d/agent-usage six follow-ups from PR 353 round 2
packages.focus: Six findings bundled in one issue. Two blocking-grade test gaps in already-correct code, mutation-proven: (1) the trap-1 guard (if (out=="") next, skips a usage snapshot with no output_tokens) has no fixture where a message.id has ONLY an interim line - add one and assert it contributes nothing to any total, and that reverting the guard makes the new test fail. (2) max_context/median_context are never asserted by key in --json output - swapping their order in flushgrp()'s printf leaves the suite green; add an assertion pinning both by key/value. Two should-fix, one a live production edge case: (3) ends_with()'s suffix match (the --pr cwd fallback) has no boundary anchor before the suffix, so a branch ending in '...-context-test' false-matches suffix 'test' as validly as '...-test' does - require the character before the match to be / or - or start-of-string. (4) <synthetic> placeholder rows (Claude Code's own internal compaction markers, legitimate zero-cost records) show as noisy all-zero-token rows with calls>0 - filter them out of output or document the phenomenon in the header comment. (5) Three doc-polish items: comment the case-insensitive project-slug match's intentionality; either uncheck PR #353's AC4 or point issue #319's description back at PR #353's explanation (check whether #319 has merged first - if not, this sub-item stays as a note in this package's own PR body rather than an edit to #319); tighten AC2's wording so scoped and unscoped cache-read percentages aren't conflated.

packages.spec: Issue 358: docker-compose.e2e.yml hardcoded host port 8443 deadlocks a worktree own dev stack
packages.focus: docker-compose.e2e.yml hardcodes ports: 8443:443 for its traefik, which collides not only with another checkout's E2E run (the single-inventory-e2e-project design already intends that) but with an ordinary dev stack in the very worktree running the gate - silently, with no clear failure message. Implement option 2 from the issue: drop the ports: block entirely and have the e2e test-runner service discover traefik's address over the compose network instead of through the host (the browser container already runs inside the same compose project and does not need a host port at all). While here, make the pre-flight check report container state (a traefik stuck in created with a non-zero exit code is not a run in progress) rather than mere existence, since #377/#389/#391 in wave 3 will build further isolation fixes on top of whatever this package ships - do not do their work, just leave the pre-flight's existing 'wait if you see a foreign container' logic in a state that a later package can extend rather than rewrite.

packages.spec: Issue 370/387/393: reviewers exhausting maxTurns and posting no verdict, on both package and consolidation diffs
packages.focus: Three reports of the same underlying failure at increasing scale, all pointing at the same fix. #370: review-docs (maxTurns 15) exhausted its budget on PR #368's round 1 with nothing posted - review-docs' step 2 is an un-narrowed repo-wide stale-doc grep (decision D9), turn-hungry by design. #393: the same failure on PR #390, a consolidation-sized diff (20 files, +3165/-52) - D2's own documented failure condition ('exits on maxTurns... a missing comment is not an approval') fired for real. #387: the general case - nine reviewer spawns were needed for six verdicts on PR #384 (H15), five of nine hit their turn limit, three could not be resumed (SendMessage returned 'No transcript found') and needed a full respawn; two specific causes identified - agents spending their last turns intending to consult the advisor rather than posting, and stalled sessions often being unresumable. Fix, combining #387's and #393's suggested directions: (1) put an explicit turn budget in all three reviewer prompts under .claude/agents stating the PR comment is the deliverable, it must be posted well before the limit, and tell reviewers NOT to call the advisor (decide this explicitly rather than leaving it implied); (2) make the spawning session (ship/SKILL.md step 5) detect 'agent returned with no verdict comment on the PR' as its own distinct state, separate from BLOCK and from not-yet-reviewed, and resume it once automatically (with the explicit-budget instruction) before counting a round; (3) size the turn budget by diff size - a consolidation-sized diff passes a raised maxTurns, mirroring how it already gets a raised round-limit (2 to 4); document this in ship/SKILL.md next to the round-limit precedent. Close #387 and #393 as each is addressed; this package's own specIssue is #370.

packages.spec: Issue 377/382/389/391: E2E gate concurrency and isolation - leftover stacks, load-induced flakes, a check-then-act race, and a machine-wide image tag
packages.focus: Opus/xhigh: four related concurrency/isolation bugs in the E2E gate, the highest-blast-radius package in this plan since every future PR's test-reviewer lane depends on this gate being trustworthy. Build on whatever #358 (wave 2) shipped for the host-port fix before starting - do not redo it. (1) #377: a finished session's stack stays Up/healthy indefinitely because nothing enforces the closing down -v; add real discriminators to the pre-flight (is there a suite runner container at all - the suite runs as run --rm e2e; has the app container logged anything in the last few minutes; does the holding worktree's .claude/worklog.md say it finished) so 'wait for it' only fires when a run is actually active, and state the teardown obligation explicitly in docker-compose.e2e.yml's header and ship/SKILL.md rather than leaving it as the last line of a sequence a session can just stop before. (2) #389: the pre-flight is a check-then-act race with a multi-minute window between reading container state and issuing down -v - implement a real lock (a lock file or a named Docker volume claimed atomically, carrying the holder's working_dir and a timestamp, with a documented way to break a stale one), ideally as a scripts/dev e2e wrapper command replacing the seven pasted compose lines in the header today. (3) #391: docker-compose.e2e.yml's image tag (inventory-e2e-app:latest) is machine-wide, so a second checkout's build silently swaps the served binary/frontend under a running suite without touching a single container - namespace the image per checkout (derive it the way working_dir already is on the containers, or stop tagging :latest), and add a cheap self-check that the served /js/* matches the working tree using the digests web/shell-manifest.json (#349) already provides, so a foreign image is an immediate legible error rather than five inexplicable test failures. (4) #382: local E2E runs are flaky under load (28 failed on an unmodified commit in one measured run) because the suite inherits CI's 12-worker fullyParallel config on a machine also running several other compose projects - cap or scale --workers for local runs, and consider a local-only Playwright retries:1 (never for CI) so a flake surfaces as a flake rather than a false red; also make the fixture-login helper's assertion distinguish a 404 (Traefik: no backend, i.e. the app was mid-restart) from a 401 (real credential rejection) so the symptom names its own cause. Update docker-compose.e2e.yml's header to stop presenting the old docker ps pre-flight as sufficient protection once the lock exists. Close #382, #389 and #391 as each is addressed; this package's own specIssue is #377.

packages.spec: Issue 371/373/379: packet all-or-nothing previous-verdict fallback, agent-usage --pr finding no calls, packet PowerShell test-file blind spot
packages.focus: Three scripts/dev.d/packet and scripts/dev.d/agent-usage follow-ups. #371: H12's 'read the PR's comment history only when the packet says it found no previous verdict comment' design (scripts/dev.d/packet:355-356) is all-or-nothing per PR, not per reviewer - a reviewer whose own round-1 comment happens to be missing (transient gh failure, race) gets no fallback signal even though the packet found other reviewers' verdicts fine. Make the fallback per-role rather than per-PR. #379: packet's 'Test files changed' heuristic does not recognise PowerShell test files, so a PR whose only tests are .ps1 reports 'Test files changed: (none)' - the single line review-tests leans on hardest - fix the file-pattern matching to include scripts/tests/*.test.ps1. #373: scripts/dev agent-usage --pr <n> returns '(no calls in range)' for a PR whose transcripts are present and countable (observed on #368), so a package issue's own acceptance criterion ('agent-usage --pr <this PR> reviewer totals in the PR body') cannot be satisfied as written - find why --pr's matching misses transcripts that --since finds and fix the mismatch. Close #373 and #379 as each is addressed; this package's own specIssue is #371.

packages.spec: Issue 372/381/429: H11 orchestrator test gaps, migrate plan internal-whitespace marker miss, the H11 stale-detector false positive
packages.focus: Three scripts/wellen-orchestrator.ps1 and internal/migrate/plan.go reliability fixes, all small self-contained test/logic additions with no intended behavior change except #429's. From #372 (four items, all in scripts/wellen-orchestrator.ps1): (1) Invoke-DoctorPreflight's Invoke-Native redirects sh's stderr to $null, so a real exec failure (not a doctor FAIL) throws an empty message - stop discarding it. (2) Register-PackageStartIfUnknown's call site in Invoke-Package's restart-meets-existing-worktree branch is untested - deleting the call leaves the suite green; add a test that catches it. (3) per-package staleAfterMinutes overriding standards.staleAfterMinutes is never asserted end-to-end - add a test that fails if the precedence is swapped. (4) Invoke-PackageRoundsBookkeeping's two WARN-and-return-null branches (no PR found; PR comments unreadable) are untested - add tests for both. #429 (this session's own earlier finding): Get-PackageLastActivity only reads branch-commit date, .claude/worklog.md's mtime, and the newest PR comment date - none of which reflect a session actively editing/testing without committing, producing false-positive staleness warnings (observed twice in the new-features wave). Add worktree file-mtime as a fourth signal (e.g. via git status --porcelain plus Get-Item on the changed paths), with a companion test alongside #372's other additions in the same file. #381: internal/migrate/plan.go's ParseClassicMarker still returns (false, nil) - silently 'no marker' - for a marker with irregular whitespace INSIDE the -- +inventory: prefix itself (e.g. '--  +inventory:classic' or '--+inventory:classic'), one level more precise than round 1's leading-whitespace/case fix; normalize internal whitespace runs before the namespace-prefix comparison, the same way trim+lower-case already handles the outer whitespace and case. Close #381 and #429 as each is addressed; this package's own specIssue is #372.

packages.spec: Issue 388/404/407/408/323: .gitignore missing patch pattern, the NAS runner untested smoke-test failure branches, two stale/fragile spec-01-and-release-workflow-test findings, and seed.sql unchecked header count
packages.focus: Five small, file-disjoint fixes, none touching product code. #388: .gitignore covers .claude/worklog.md, *.log, *.diff, *.txt and *.md but not *.patch - a review agent's scratch .claude/test-diff.patch has landed on main once already (H15, #384); add .claude/*.patch next to the existing *.diff line. #404: deploy/synology/runner/entrypoint.sh's smoke_test() (five checks: docker-compose version floor, git present, Docker socket answers, clone-path match, compose files parse; collect-rather-than-short-circuit) has no test of any failure branch, only the happy path via the runner-image CI job - add deploy/synology/runner/entrypoint_test.go (or extend cmd/inventory/runner_compose_test.go) in the shape deploy/synology/update_test.go already establishes: drive entrypoint.sh with RUNNER_SMOKE_ONLY=1 and a stub PATH, vary what is missing/broken, and assert the exit code is 1 and a multi-fault run names every fault, not just the first. #407: docs/specs/01-architecture-and-deployment.md's 'Deployment model' section (~line 900) still says deploying is the manual procedure 'until [spec 38's packages] land' - they have (H14/H15/H16/H17), and spec 18 already got the equivalent fix in PR #406; rewrite spec 01's copy the same way (an ordinary release is scripts/dev release <tag>, manual is the fallback for a runner-down NAS). #408: scripts/release_workflow_test.go's TestReleaseDeployRunsOnlyWhenTheGateAndBothCallsPassed matches !cancelled() with plain strings.Contains over the whole file, so the guard string also matching inside an explanatory comment means deleting the live guard on line ~216 leaves the test green - strip #-comment lines before matching (the same helper pattern TestReleaseIsTheOnlyWorkflowNamingASelfHostedRunner and TestReleaseWorkflowNeverChecksOutTheRepository already use in the same file) and reuse it for every guard-string assertion in that file. #323: e2e/fixtures/seed.sql's header states a row count that has drifted silently twice with nothing checking it (docs/specs/05-frontend-pwa-foundations.md deliberately stopped restating the count itself, per #239, making the header the single remaining source of truth) - add a check that fails when the header's numbers stop matching the file, preferably a query in the E2E suite asserting count(*) from users/storages against the header's numbers after seeding (catches an ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING silent collision too, not just a stale comment). Close #404, #407, #408 and #323 as each is addressed; this package's own specIssue is #388.
